title: How JoyoRogo works out your eating target
subtitle: From BMR and activity level to the extra movement your watch or phone measures. With a worked example and sources.

why.title: BMR and TDEE: what is the difference
why.p1: BMR is the energy your body uses at complete rest: breathing, heartbeat, keeping warm. It is worked out from your weight, height, age and sex with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation (1990).
why.p2: TDEE is the total energy you burn in a day: BMR plus everyday movement plus the energy of digesting food. Eat your TDEE and your weight stays the same. JoyoRogo's eating target starts from TDEE, then subtracts a deficit to lose weight (or adds a surplus to gain).
why.p3: It used to start from BMR alone. That is too low for almost everyone, because it has no daily movement and no energy of digesting food in it.

formula.title: TDEE = BMR × factor
formula.p1: TDEE is BMR times an activity factor, standard numbers in wide use, from 1.2 to 1.9 depending on how active your days are. You choose the level.
formula.p2: Digesting and absorbing food also costs energy, called the thermic effect of food (TEF): about 5 to 15% of daily expenditure (Westerterp 2004), and JoyoRogo uses 10%. It is already inside the factor, because the factors come from total expenditure. That is why TEF is not added again.
formula.chart: Example for the {{level}} level (factor {{factor}}): TDEE is made of BMR, the daily movement already in the factor, and the effect of eating.
formula.chartLabel: Stacked bar: BMR {{bmr}} kcal, daily movement {{move}} kcal, effect of eating {{tef}} kcal, total TDEE {{tdee}} kcal.

levels.title: Five activity levels
levels.intro: Each level has a standard factor. Here is what it means, an example, and how big its TDEE is for the example below.
levels.tip: Between two levels? Pick the lower one, then see whether your weight drops as planned. The app also suggests a level from your steps and from your weight trend (see below).
levels.chart: The higher the level, the bigger the TDEE. The solid part is the BMR, the same for every level.
levels.chartLabel: Bar chart of the TDEE for all five levels.

credit.title: Your watch and phone only add, never subtract
credit.p1: Your factor already contains an average day of movement. So data from your watch, phone or Health is not counted from zero: only the measured movement that goes beyond what your factor already contains counts.
credit.p2: Movement already in the factor = TDEE − BMR − 10% of TDEE (the effect of eating). For the {{level}} example that is about {{included}} kcal.
credit.p3: The extra is multiplied by the percentage you set (default {{pct}}%) and the daily addition is capped (default {{cap}} kcal). The percentage is below 100 because wrist devices are not accurate for energy: of 7 devices tested, none got its error below 20% (Shcherbina et al. 2017). Workouts you log outside the watch's total, for example by hand, are added the same way.
credit.chart: Three example days for the {{level}} level. The dashed line is the movement already in the factor ({{included}} kcal). Only the part above the line counts.
credit.chartLabel: Chart of three days: measured movement {{a}}, {{b}} and {{c}} kcal against the {{included}} kcal line.
credit.legendBelow: Already in the factor, not added
credit.deskTitle: A phone left on a desk
credit.deskBody: A tiny number from a phone that was not carried is no longer read as a quiet day. If the measured movement is below what your factor already contains, the addition is zero and your target stays the base target. Your target never drops because of watch or phone data.

recommend.title: Suggestions to be more accurate
recommend.intro: Your level is your best guess. These two help check it. Both are only suggestions with a Use button, never applied on their own.
recommend.stepsBody: If your account has step data on at least 5 of the last 14 days, the average is matched to the Tudor-Locke & Bassett (2004) step index. In onboarding this suggestion only shows when the data already exists.
recommend.trendBody: After at least 3 weeks of regular weigh-ins and food logging (70% of days logged), JoyoRogo works out what your body really burns: what you ate on average, adjusted for your weight change, minus the average of your logged workouts. That is divided by your BMR and matched to the nearest level. You see the measured number against the formula's.
recommend.trendNote: The 7,700 kcal per kg rule is only an approximation, because the body adapts as weight changes (Hall et al. 2011). So this is a suggestion, not a verdict.

example.title: Worked example
example.intro: Male, 26 years, 171.5 cm, 107.7 kg, target 78 kg by 4 June 2027, worked out on 19 October 2026. BMR = 10 × 107.7 + 6.25 × 171.5 − 5 × 26 + 5 = {{bmr}} kcal. The deficit needed is {{raw}} kcal a day, capped at {{deficit}}.
example.floorNote: At the lowest level, TDEE minus the deficit falls under the minimum eating floor for men ({{floor}} kcal), so the target is {{floor}} kcal.
example.oldNote: The old model (BMR minus the deficit) gave {{old}} kcal for every level.
